question: As per State of the Judiciary Report 2023, women constitute ______ of the working strength of the district judiciary.
solution:
The correct answer is __**36.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **State of the Judiciary Report 2023**, women constitute **36.3%** of the working strength of the district judiciary in India.
 
• The report highlights the gender disparity in the judiciary, emphasizing that although women are increasingly represented, the overall ratio still remains skewed.
 
• District judiciary plays a pivotal role in the justice delivery system as it deals with a majority of the cases in India, making gender representation crucial for equitable justice.
 
• This data reflects progress in gender inclusion but also indicates the need for policies promoting higher representation of women in the judiciary.
 
• The percentage of women in the district judiciary is higher compared to the representation of women in the higher judiciary, including High Courts and the Supreme Court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State of the Judiciary Report:**

 
 
• The **State of the Judiciary Report** is an annual publication that provides insights into the functioning, efficiency, and representation within the judiciary system in India.
 
• It evaluates various aspects such as gender disparity, case pendency, infrastructure challenges, and judicial reforms.
 
• The report aims to promote transparency and accountability in the judicial system.
 
 
 
• **Representation of Women in Judiciary:**
 
 
• Despite the increase in women representation, the overall percentage of female judges in India remains low, especially in higher judiciary institutions.
 
• Efforts are being made to increase gender diversity through initiatives like reservation for women in judicial services exams.
 
• The judiciary has witnessed landmark appointments, such as **Justice Indira Banerjee** in the Supreme Court, reflecting gradual progress.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by Women in Judiciary:**
 
 
• Women often face challenges such as societal prejudice, lack of mentorship, and work-life balance issues.
 
• Infrastructure in courts often lacks gender-friendly facilities, which can discourage women from pursuing a career in law.
 
• There is a need for policy reforms to encourage and support women in judicial roles.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Reforms in India:**
 
 
• Judicial reforms aim to improve efficiency, accessibility, and inclusivity within the Indian judicial system.
 
• Key reforms include digitization of court records, fast-track courts for specific cases, and promotion of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms.
 
• Efforts are also being made to address gender disparity through awareness programs and policy interventions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **District Judiciary:**

 
 
• District judiciary forms the backbone of the Indian judicial system and deals with a majority of the cases across the country.
 
• It includes civil courts, criminal courts, and family courts, among others, at the district level.
 
• Judicial officers at the district level are recruited through state judiciary exams conducted by respective High Courts.
 
 
 
• **Gender Representation in Higher Judiciary:**
 
 
• Women representation in the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** is significantly lower compared to district courts.
 
• The appointment of female judges has been a topic of discussion, with calls for more equitable representation.
 
• In 2021, three women judges were appointed to the Supreme Court, marking a progressive step in gender representation.
 
 
 
• **Initiatives to Promote Women in Judiciary:**
 
 
• Several state governments have introduced gender-based reservations for women in judicial services exams.
 
• Training programs and workshops are being organized to encourage women to pursue careers in law and judiciary.
 
• Awareness campaigns aim to change societal perceptions regarding women in leadership roles within the judiciary.
